The text defines Q = {p prime : p | A} and sigma(x) = P(x) ∩ Q (and asserts 'Only the primes dividing A can matter here'). Take A = 15, so Q = {3,5}. The sequence is 15, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 40, 42, ... (terms ≥ 15 divisible by at least two of 2,3,5). For the term x = 18, all prime factors (2, 3) are ≤ 15, yet sigma(18) = {3} ≠ P(18) = {2,3}, so the quoted step is false. Moreover sigma(18) = {3} is not good, since the term 20 is coprime to 3; so the Lemma's conclusion fails. Downstream, L = ∏_{p∈Q} p = 15 and T = #terms in [15,29] = 4 give a_6 = 36 ≠ a_2 + 15 = 33, so (4) and the boxed identity are false under the stated definitions.
